topic: Yamato's entire defiance of Kaidou is built on one page in Oden's logbook
title: Yamato's War With Kaidou Is Built On One Page
description: Yamato's entire identity as Oden comes from one logbook he found by a stream twenty years ago. What if Oda never wrote the one page that turns it into a war with Kaidou? From the full story: What If Oden Never Opened Wano's Borders?
comment: Is Yamato's loyalty to Oden about the man, or about finishing his mission? Pick one.

lines.text: Yamato's whole war with Kaidou is built on one page in a logbook.

shot.fallback: young warrior holding a worn journal, resolute

lines.text: What if Oda never wrote that page at all?

shot.fallback: blank journal page where writing should be

lines.text: In chapter 968, Oden hears a prophecy at sea and decides to open Wano's borders.

shot.fallback: samurai staring at the horizon from a ship

lines.text: Twenty years later, Yamato finds that exact promise inside Oden's own journal.

shot.fallback: child discovering a journal by a stream

lines.text: He calls it his bible, and builds his whole identity around finishing it.

shot.fallback: young warrior reading a journal intently

lines.text: Erase that one line, and Yamato still becomes Oden in every other way.

shot.fallback: warrior adopting a legendary samurai's stance

lines.text: Same posture. Same name. Same refusal to ever bow to his own father.

shot.fallback: warrior standing defiantly before a towering figure

lines.text: What he loses is the reason it was ever about more than himself.
When Kaidou offers him the shogun's seat, Yamato still says no.

shot.fallback: dragon pirate offering a throne to a young warrior

lines.text: Not for Wano this time. Just because it's still his own life.
Because without that one page, the only thing holding up his whole war with Kaidou...

shot.fallback: warrior standing alone against a towering dragon pirate
